issues.issue: The definition refers to "the Borrowing of which such Loan is a part" although no Loan has been mentioned in the sentence, leaving the antecedent missing. The date on which interest falls due therefore has to be inferred.

The enumeration runs "(i) ... and (iii)" with no clause (ii), and the following proviso restarts at "(a), (b), (c)" although the definition already uses (a) and (b) as its main limbs. A clause appears to have dropped out of the operative mechanism for subsequent Borrowings.

Limb (b) opens "the sum of (i) ..." but never numbers a second element, running straight into "plus the aggregate amount of all LC Disbursements". The broken enumeration obscures what a single Lender's LC Exposure comprises.

The definition limits "Lender" to assignees that become "a Project Lender", a term the Recitals define to include providers of supplier's credit rather than only term lenders. The two definitions pull in different directions on who can be a Lender.

The closing words "on the same terms as the required by the Loans" are grammatically incomplete, so the condition on which items (ii) and (iii) enter the denominator cannot be applied as written. The Lender's entire prepayment share turns on that clause.

Unlike the parallel "Upstream Supplier Financing Creditor's Pro Rata Interest" and "Additional Indebtedness Holder's Pro Rata Interest" definitions, this one omits the "(and not an optional prepayment)" qualifier and cites Section 2.11(b) rather than 2.11(f). The three shares of one pro rata allocation are not drafted consistently.

The definition caps expiry at the earlier of 36 months from issuance or four years from the date of the Agreement (29 December 2014), yet clause (4) permits negotiation as late as 30 December 2014. The two internal deadlines cannot both be met.

Letters of Credit may be issued to 30 June 2013 and drawn long afterwards, but Section 2.06(e) converts every LC Disbursement into a Term Loan while Section 2.01 provides that undrawn Term Loan Commitments "lapse automatically" at the end of the Term Loan Availability Period on 30 September 2013. How a Term Loan arises after that lapse is unexplained.

The rate is taken from the Reuters "LIBOR01" screen, while the "Market Disruption Event" definition tests availability of the Reuters "LIBO01" screen rate. The two definitions identify the reference source differently.

After a closed list of named instruments the definition adds "any other document designated from time to time as a Loan Document by the Lenders or the Facility Agent", allowing one side unilaterally to expand the category. The scope of that catch-all against the enumerated documents is open to construction.

Limb (a) sweeps in "deferred payment guaranties, shortfall undertakings or payment undertakings or any nature whatsoever", a garbled catch-all (apparently for "of any nature") whose reach beyond the named categories is undefined. It sits directly against the specific instruments listed before it.

Each limb depends on what "Required Lenders determine", including limb (iii)'s cost of matching deposits and limb (iv)'s availability of deposits, with no objectivity or good-faith standard. The lenders' own determination decides whether the pricing basis disappears.

"Material adverse effect on ... the business, financial condition, operations or performance or properties of the Borrower since March 31, 2010" fixes neither a measure of materiality nor a coherent comparison date. Material adverse effect language of this kind is the standard subject of construction fights.

"[A]ll material approvals and consents by any Person" is bounded only by an "including, but not limited to" list, so the class of approvals whose absence breaches the conditions is indeterminate. "Material" is not defined.

The arithmetic is garbled — "the sum of (A) ... minus, (B) ... and (C) minus mark-to-market amounts" — so it is unclear whether (C) is added or subtracted, and the US$25,000,000 test's referent is equally unclear. A financial covenant computed on this formula cannot be applied with confidence.

The tax deduction refers to "any such event in respect of any Foreign Subsidiary", but "Foreign Subsidiary" is undefined and the "Subsidiary" definition records that the Borrower has none. The limb has no operative referent in this instrument.

Both limbs close "in each case to the extent arising in connection with the Obligations", so the definition of Obligations is expressed by reference to itself. The circularity leaves the secured perimeter to be worked out by construction.

"Obligor" means "any of the Borrowers or any Guarantor", using a plural that does not exist: "Borrower" is defined as the single entity Essar Steel Minnesota LLC. The mismatch is a drafting slip on the face of the definition.

Several limbs turn on undefined materiality tests — Liens that "secure amounts that are not material to the value of the properties to which such Liens attach" and encumbrances that do not "materially adversely affect the value" — and the closing proviso reads "any Lien securing Indebtedness on Attributable Debt". The permitted-lien perimeter is not fixed by the words.

Limb (e) permits repurchase agreements "with a maturity not less than one (1) year thereafter", the opposite of the short-maturity limit applied to every other permitted investment. On its face the words admit the least liquid instruments in a liquidity definition.

Three stacked provisos alternately require and dispense with the Required Lenders' prior written consent for de-bottlenecking and similar modifications, so whether consent is needed depends on how the exceptions interact. The opening words already require consent, which the second proviso then removes in defined circumstances.

The sentence "includes any Permitted Project Change subject to the receipt of approval, if any, required in the definition of Permitted Project Change has been approved as set forth in the definition of that term" is ungrammatical and doubles back on itself. Whether an unapproved change falls within the Project cannot be read off the words.

The definition carves out contracts below a US$4,000,000 "Contract Threshold" and those listed on Schedule 1.01E, then requires "commercially reasonable efforts" to obtain consents even for the excluded ones, and then redefines the term again for Sections 6.09 and 6.10. Which contracts are "Project Contracts" therefore varies by provision and by an unmeasured efforts standard.

The Recitals define "Project Lenders" to include providers of supplier's credit as well as the Initial Lender and Subsequent Project Lenders, whereas the operative provisions (for example "Cash Sweep Debt Service" and "Lender") use the term as if it meant term loan lenders only. The recital definition and the operative use do not sit together.

Limbs (a) and (b) describe two overlapping periods — the fiscal year and a rolling half-year straddle — with no "or", "and" or rule for choosing between them. Which period a financial test is measured over is left open.
